title: 第3章 崇明足球基地第4章 情若父子
content_zh:
第三章 崇明足球基地
“你踢球很厉害？”，那个林姓警察听高军说想去崇明足球基地后当即问道，毕竟崇明足球基地虽然收费是全国最低的，但也同样是要收费的，而高军现在连监护人都没有，又哪儿有钱来付学费？除非天赋足够出色，徐指导才会自掏腰包，毕竟他搞基地可不是为了做慈善......
“在大屏幕上看过，甲A球员的水平看上去也不怎么样，我觉得我也能够做到。”，高军这样答道。
“你可真是无知者无畏。”，林姓警察闻言笑道，不过正好他这个周末有场野球可踢，于是便决定干脆将高军带过去上场踢踢看，不行的话也没损失，正好劝他打消这个不现实的念头，如果真的那么有天赋，那么正好帮局里解决掉这个小麻烦，而且作为一个中国足球的铁杆支持者，他心底里其实也一直渴望着中国能够出一个真正的足球天才......
虽然高军退役后就很少踢球了，但毕竟底子深厚，穿越前四十多岁的时候在训练中随便一脚射门依然能够令某个世界名教惊呼“真像苏克”，可见其射术精湛到了何种地步。虽然现在这具年幼的身体仅有不到1米4的身高，而且十分瘦弱，并且刚刚穿越过来还不是十分熟悉，但是对付一些纯业余水平的大叔，高军还是觉得没有任何难度......
虽然一开始业余比赛常见的“球在天上飞”给了身材矮小的高军很大的困扰，但是当他发现这具新身体的动作频率颇为出色，当年并不以突破过人而闻名的高军立即来了一次“过五关斩六将”，带球杀到门将跟前轻轻一推，皮球就从那个大胖子的档下穿入了网内......
“厉害！太厉害了，我家那小子连你的一半、不、是四分之一都比不上，即使他那队里技术最好的，与你一比也什么都不是......”，一个家里小孩就在崇明基地学习踢球的大叔喘着粗气坐倒在地上，一脸不敢置信地看着高军，缓过气来后又接着补了一句，“你不去踢球，绝对是中国足球的损失......”
而这时的高军却在默默回味着刚才那种连续变速变向、不需要假动作都可以将防守球员随意玩弄的惬意感觉，“这就是天赋吗？”
直到高军穿越的时候，绝大多数中国教练关注的身体素质当中依然只有传统的身高、力量、速度，最多再加上耐力、爆发力和弹跳，很少有人重视动作频率、或者说灵活性，以及平衡性等不太直观的“隐性”身体素质，这一点甚至还不如很多FM游戏的玩家。
但事实上灵活性与平衡性都是十分重要的，后者是持球对抗的根本，平衡不好的人就算身体再壮、在对方的贴身防守下也很难保证技术动作不变形，处理脚下球时尤其如此，这个问题上最典型的反面典型就是山东的那位“中国第一高中锋”韩大鸟，而且平衡性好的人不容易被假动作晃到，自己也能够作出动作幅度更大的假动作而产生更大的欺骗性，因此无论是对进攻球员还是对防守球员来说都十分重要。
高军在当国足主帅的时候曾经专门研究过日本队，发现他们的球员虽然没有中国的人高马大，但是平衡性却普遍优于中国队的球员，因此拿球很稳、不怕逼抢，实战中他们的传切配合特别出色应该与此有很大的关系。再加上日本球队风格统一的优势有利于默契的形成，因此虽然其实中国球员个人技术与日本球员的差距并没有那么大，但比赛中的表现看上去却像是差了两个档次。说到底，这还是由于中国的青训教练在选材时更加重视身高、力量、速度这种一眼就能看出的素质，而忽视类似平衡性这样的“隐性”身体素质所致。
而比起平衡性，小球员的动作频率、特别是步频甚至更加重要，因为小时候绝对速度快、长大后未必还能保持优势，而一个步频超快的小孩长大后，只要个子不太矮（腿不太短）、肌肉类型也不是以爆发力很差的慢缩红肌为主，速度就肯定慢不了。
之所以这样，是因为一个人的动作频率在很小的时候就定下来了，甚至可以理解成是天生的，因此小时候动作频率快、长大后也一定快（个子长高后动作频率相对自己小时候肯定会减慢，但与同等身高的其他人相比，一般仍能保有小时候的优势。），而平衡性的情况也差不多。与之相比，个子矮、块头小、甚至速度慢这些缺陷却都可能随着年龄的增大而改变，尤其是国内青少年球员改年龄的歪风更是增大了青训教练看走眼的可能性，而如果围绕那些较早定型的素质来选材，小球员最终的成材率无疑会提高很多。
因此，也难怪高军发现自己动作频率很快后会那么高兴了，而且记忆中这个小孩的父亲不算矮，这就进一步确保了高军日后的绝对速度。虽说对于一个前锋来说，爆发力在某些时候比绝对速度更加重要，但是绝对速度快与爆发力并不矛盾，两者反而是相辅相成的关系，所以对同一个球员来说，速度肯定是越快越好。更何况足球比赛中相当一部分的进球都是在反击中打进的，这个时候绝对速度就更加重要了......
得知高军足球天赋惊人后，那个公安局的局长也很高兴，一是他自己同样是足球迷，二是终于可以摆脱这个麻烦了。心情大好的局长甚至还在局里搞了次募捐，帮助高军筹到了两三千块钱的生活费，此外还让那个林姓警员送高军去崇明。高军连连推却不过，最后只得接受了警察们的好意，想到可以重新踏上绿茵场，他的心里不禁充满了喜悦和激动，就连自己很可能再也见不到父母妻儿的痛苦也不觉淡去了许多......
content_en:
Chapter 3 Chongming Football Base
"Are you good at football?" the policeman surnamed Lin asked immediately after hearing Gao Jun say he wanted to go to Chongming Football Base. After all, although Chongming Football Base has the lowest fees in the country, it still charges fees. And Gao Jun doesn't even have a guardian now, so how can he have the money to pay for the tuition? Unless the talent is outstanding enough, Director Xu will pay out of his own pocket. After all, he does not set up the base for charity...
"I've seen it on the big screen, and the level of A-A players doesn't look that good. I think I can do it," Gao Jun replied.
"You are really ignorant and fearless." The policeman surnamed Lin laughed when he heard this, but he happened to have a wild ball to play this weekend, so he decided to simply take Gao Jun over to play.
Although Gao Jun rarely plays football after retiring, he has a solid foundation after all. When he was in his forties before time travel, a random shot in training could still make a world-famous coach exclaim "really like Su Ke", which shows how superb his shooting skills are. Although this young body is now less than 1.4 meters tall, very thin, and is not very familiar with it just after time travel, Gao Jun still finds it not difficult to deal with some uncles who are purely amateurs...
Although the "ball flying in the sky" common in amateur games troubled the short Gao Jun a lot at the beginning, when he discovered that the frequency of movements of this new body was quite good, Gao Jun, who was not known for his breakthroughs at the time, immediately came to "pass five levels and kill six generals". He drove the ball to the goalkeeper and pushed it gently, and the ball penetrated the net from under the big fat man...
"Awesome! So awesome. That boy of mine can't even compare to half, no, a quarter of you. Even if he has the best skills in the team, he is nothing compared to you..." An uncle whose children were learning football at the Chongming base gasped and sat down on the ground. He looked at Gao Jun in disbelief. After regaining his breath, he added, "If you don't play football, it will definitely be a loss for Chinese football..."
At this time, Gao Jun was silently reminiscing about the pleasant feeling of continuously changing speed and direction, and being able to play with the defensive players at will without any fake moves, "Is this talent?"
Until the time when Gao Jun traveled through time, the physical qualities that most Chinese coaches paid attention to were still traditional height, strength, and speed, plus endurance, explosive power, and jumping at most. Few people paid attention to less intuitive "hidden" physical qualities such as frequency of movement, flexibility, and balance. This is even worse than that of many FM game players.
But in fact, both flexibility and balance are very important. The latter is the basis of confrontation with the ball. No matter how strong a person is, it will be difficult for a person with poor balance to ensure that his technical movements are not deformed under the close defense of the opponent. This is especially true when handling the ball at his feet. This is the most typical negative example of this issue. It is Shandong's "China's No. 1 High Center Forward" Han Daniao. People with good balance are not easily swayed by fake moves, and they can also make fake moves with a wider range of movements to create greater deception. Therefore, it is very important for both offensive players and defensive players.
Gao Jun once studied the Japanese team when he was the national football coach and found that although their players are not as tall as the Chinese players, their balance is generally better than that of the Chinese team's players. Therefore, they are very stable with the ball and are not afraid of pressing. In actual combat, their passing and cutting coordination is particularly good, which should have a lot to do with this.Big relationship. In addition, the advantage of the Japanese team's unified style is conducive to the formation of tacit understanding. Therefore, although the gap between Chinese players' personal skills and Japanese players is not that big, the performance in the game seems to be two levels behind. In the final analysis, this is because China's youth training coaches pay more attention to qualities that can be seen at a glance such as height, strength, and speed when selecting talents, while ignoring "hidden" physical qualities such as balance.
Compared with balance, the frequency of movements of young players, especially the cadence, is even more important, because the absolute speed in childhood may not be able to maintain the advantage when they grow up. And when a child with an ultra-fast cadence grows up, as long as he is not too short (the legs are not too short) and the muscle type is not dominated by slow-twitch red muscles with poor explosive power, the speed will definitely not be slow.
The reason for this is because a person's movement frequency is determined at a very young age, and can even be understood as innate. Therefore, the movement frequency is fast when he is a child, and it will definitely be faster when he grows up (when he grows taller, his movement frequency will definitely slow down compared to his childhood, but compared with other people of the same height, he can generally still maintain the advantage he had when he was a child.), and the balance situation is similar. In contrast, shortcomings such as short stature, small size, and even slow speed may change with age. In particular, the trend of domestic young players changing their age increases the possibility of youth training coaches making mistakes. If the selection is based on those qualities that were finalized earlier, the final success rate of young players will undoubtedly increase a lot.
Therefore, it is no wonder that Gao Jun was so happy when he discovered that his movements were very fast, and in his memory, the child's father was not short, which further ensured Gao Jun's absolute speed in the future. Although for a forward, explosive power is sometimes more important than absolute speed, absolute speed and explosive power are not contradictory. Instead, the two are complementary. Therefore, for the same player, the faster the better. What's more, a large number of goals in football matches are scored during counterattacks. At this time, absolute speed is even more important...
After learning that Gao Jun's football talent was amazing, the director of the Public Security Bureau was also very happy. First, he was also a football fan, and second, he could finally get rid of this trouble. The director, who was in a good mood, even held a fundraiser in the bureau and helped Gao Jun raise two to three thousand yuan for living expenses. In addition, he asked the police officer surnamed Lin to send Gao Jun to Chongming. Gao Jun refused repeatedly, but finally had to accept the police's kindness. Thinking of being able to set foot on the green field again, his heart couldn't help but be filled with joy and excitement. Even the pain that he would probably never see his parents, wife and children again felt a lot less...
